# Model and source

Badhan et al. (2017) applied pharmacokinetic modelling to a cationic liposomal
subunit-tuberculosis vaccine: the two-component adjuvant DDA:TDB
(dimethyldioctadecylammonium bromide + trehalose 6,6-dibehenate, the CAF01
system) carrying the Ag85B-ESAT-6 (H1) subunit antigen, administered
intramuscularly in mice. A dual radiolabel (liposome tracked with 3-H, antigen
with 125-I) gave injection-site and draining-lymph-node biodistribution at 1, 4
and 14 days. The authors fit two kinds of model: empirical compartmental models
of the injection-site kinetics (Table 2), and a minimal, semi-mechanistic PBPK
model (Equations 7-10) later extrapolated to a 71 kg human.

**This vignette ships the two empirical compartmental models**, which are fully
and cleanly reproducible from Table 2. The minimal-PBPK model is described
below with the reasons it is not shipped as a packaged model (see *The
minimal-PBPK model* and *Assumptions and deviations*).

* Citation: `r readModelDb("Badhan_2017_liposome_mouse_1cmt")()$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics9040057> (PMCID PMC5750663)

| File | Class | Molecule | Source |
|------|-------|----------|--------|
| `Badhan_2017_liposome_mouse_1cmt` | empirical 1-cmt | DDA:TDB liposome | Eq 1, Table 2 |
| `Badhan_2017_antigen_mouse_2cmt` | empirical 2-cmt | Ag85B-ESAT-6 antigen | Eq 2-3, Table 2 |

# Population

The data are mouse (28 g) biodistribution profiles of a dual radio-labelled
DDA:TDB liposome (250 ug DDA + 50 ug TDB) adsorbing 2 ug of Ag85B-ESAT-6 (H1)
antigen, injected IM in 50 uL and sampled at the site of injection and draining
lymph nodes at 1, 4 and 14 days (plus a 0.25-day in-vitro point). The models are
deterministic: a best-fit model was selected by AIC and only point estimates are
reported (no inter-individual variability or residual error).

```{r population}
readModelDb("Badhan_2017_liposome_mouse_1cmt")()$population$disease_state
```

# Source trace

The injection-site ("central") kinetics were fit with a 1-, 2- or
3-compartment model (Equations 1-6) and selected by AIC: a 1-compartment model
for the liposome and a 2-compartment model for the antigen (Table 2). The
central compartment is the quadriceps site of injection; `k10` is the
first-order loss from that site and `k12`/`k21` the antigen distribution
micro-constants. No volume was reported, so the packaged models use an apparent
volume of 1 and `Cc` is the site-of-injection amount.

| Parameter | Liposome (1-cmt) | Antigen (2-cmt) | Source |
|-----------|------------------|------------------|--------|
| k10 | 0.0306 /day | 0.34 /day | Table 2 |
| k12 | - | 22.26 /day | Table 2 |
| k21 | - | 77.58 /day | Table 2 |
| distribution t1/2 (alpha) | - | 0.0069 day | Table 2 |
| terminal t1/2 (beta) | 22.6 day | 2.62 day | Table 2 |
| MRT | 32.6 day | 3.78 day | Table 2 |

# Injection-site kinetics (replicates Table 2 / Figure 3)

The liposome persists at the muscle depot (terminal half-life 22.6 days) while
the antigen is cleared an order of magnitude faster (terminal half-life 2.62
days), the central finding of the compartmental analysis.

```{r profiles}
sim_cmt <- function(model_name, dose, cmt = "central", tmax = 60) {
  mod <- readModelDb(model_name)
  ev <- et(amt = dose, cmt = cmt) |> et(seq(0, tmax, by = 0.1))
  rxSolve(mod, ev, returnType = "data.frame")
}
lip <- sim_cmt("Badhan_2017_liposome_mouse_1cmt", dose = 300)
ant <- sim_cmt("Badhan_2017_antigen_mouse_2cmt", dose = 2)

prof <- bind_rows(
  transform(lip[, c("time", "Cc")], molecule = "Liposome", pct = lip$Cc / 300 * 100),
  transform(ant[, c("time", "Cc")], molecule = "Antigen", pct = ant$Cc / 2 * 100)
)
ggplot(prof, aes(time, pct, colour = molecule)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "% of dose remaining at injection site (log scale)",
       colour = NULL, title = "Injection-site kinetics: liposome vs antigen (Table 2)") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Half-life checks (Table 2)

```{r halflife}
hl <- function(s, t_a, t_b) {
  ca <- approx(s$time, s$Cc, t_a)$y
  cb <- approx(s$time, s$Cc, t_b)$y
  log(2) / (log(ca / cb) / (t_b - t_a))
}
lip_hl <- hl(lip, 10, 40)
ant_hl <- hl(ant, 5, 15)
cat(sprintf("Liposome 1-cmt terminal t1/2 = %.1f day (Table 2: 22.6)\n", lip_hl))
cat(sprintf("Antigen  2-cmt terminal t1/2 = %.2f day (Table 2: 2.62)\n", ant_hl))

stopifnot(
  abs(lip_hl - 22.6) < 1.0,
  abs(ant_hl - 2.62) < 0.2
)
```

The antigen distribution (alpha) half-life is governed by the fast
`k12`/`k21` exchange; the early concentration drop reproduces the reported
`t1/2alpha` of 0.0069 day.

```{r alpha-halflife}
ant_fast <- sim_cmt("Badhan_2017_antigen_mouse_2cmt", dose = 2, tmax = 0.1)
cat(sprintf("Antigen central amount drops from %.3f (t=0) to %.3f by t=0.02 d\n",
            ant_fast$Cc[1], approx(ant_fast$time, ant_fast$Cc, 0.02)$y))
```

# The minimal-PBPK model (described, not shipped)

The paper's headline contribution is a four-compartment minimal-PBPK model
(muscle, popliteal lymph node (PLN), rest of body, plasma; Figure 2,
Equations 7-10) with mouse and human physiology (Table 1) and tissue
degradation constants (Table 4, mouse only), extrapolated to a human antigen
prediction. The maintainers evaluated it carefully and did **not** package it,
for three reasons:

1. **The printed equations are dimensionally inconsistent.** Equations 7-10 are
   written with a `V * dA/dt` left-hand side while the loss terms are
   `rate * concentration`, so the units do not close, and the transvascular
   flux definition `tv_tissue = Q_tissue / V_tissue * fe` admits several
   readings.

2. **The PLN compartment cannot be reproduced.** Across every plausible reading
   of the equations the muscle depot reproduces the paper well (e.g. the human
   deltoid Cmax is approximately dose / deltoid volume, matching the reported
   0.25 ug/mL), but the popliteal-lymph-node concentration comes out
   10^3-10^4 times the reported value, with the wrong time of maximum. The
   authors themselves report the PLN as their least reliable prediction
   (precision errors up to 74%, Table 3).

3. **The human degradation constant is unreported.** Table 4 tabulates `kdeg`
   for the mouse only. Reproducing the reported human muscle half-life of 13.2
   days requires `kdeg,muscle` near 0.05/day, whereas the tabulated mouse antigen
   value (0.320/day) gives about 2.2 days; no human `kdeg` exists in the paper
   or any supplement (there is no supplement and no deposited code).

A faithful, reproducible packaged model therefore could not be built for the
minimal-PBPK arm from the on-disk sources, so only the compartmental models
(which are exact) are shipped.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Scope (operator ruling, 2026-11-25).** Only the two empirical compartmental
  models (Table 2) are packaged. The minimal-PBPK model is documented above and
  not shipped, because it is not reproducible from the printed equations (see
  the three reasons above): dimensional inconsistency, a PLN compartment off by
  ~10^4x, and an unreported human degradation constant.

* **Apparent volume.** The Table 2 models report only rate constants (no
  volume), so the packaged files use an apparent volume of 1; `Cc` is the
  site-of-injection amount and only the half-lives and profile shapes are
  meaningful.

* **No variability.** A single best-fit model was selected by AIC and only point
  estimates are reported; the models are deterministic (no IIV, no residual
  error).
```
